subject: Weekly MAP benchmarking sync — latency & throughput results
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Brian Sanders <brian.sanders@sigmahealth.com>, Emily Chen <emily.chen@sigmahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Weekly MAP benchmarking sync — latency & throughput results

Hi Brian / Emily,

Attached are the initial numbers from this week's run against the mid-traffic MAP set (end-to-end p95 latency and aggregate throughput across 5m windows). High-level: throughput looks on-track vs the MAP target, but p95 spikes on tails for the longer sequences. We broke results down by model variant and batching config — see sigma_latency_report_v1.csv (attached) and the suggested binary patch to the batching policy redwood_batching_config.patch.

Agenda for today's quick checkpoint (15 minutes):
- Share numbers (5m) and highlight p95 spikes
- Agree on tuning plan for the long-sequence tail (owners + timeline)
- Decide whether to swap to compressed kv-cache in the canary for the next 24h

Ask: please confirm availability for a 15-minute sync at 10:30 PT. If you can't make it, we'll capture action items here and follow up.

Notes inside the attachments: CSV has p50/p95/p99, throughput by model (redwood-1b/4b/8b-quant), and request shape distribution. Quick summary:
- Aggregate throughput: 2.8k req/min (target 2.5k)
- p95 (all): 410ms (target <= 350ms) — long-sequence cohort p95 = 780ms
- p50 = 110ms

Next steps I propose if we hit the same pattern in the canary:
1) Short-term: enable prefix caching for >512 token flows on dedicated canary (owner: Dev, target: 24h)
2) Mid-term: increase batching window by 15ms for 8b quant variant and test for latency regressions (owner: Marissa, target: 72h)
3) If p95 remains >500ms, fall back to the 4b variant for long sequences for the close window (owner: Rishi)

Attachments: sigma_latency_report_v1.csv, redwood_batching_config.patch, map-weekly-notes-20260615.pdf

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Head of Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Brian Sanders <brian.sanders@sigmahealth.com>, Emily Chen <emily.chen@sigmahealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 09:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Weekly MAP benchmarking sync — latency & throughput results

Neha — thanks for the summary and the attachments. Quick read-through notes:
- The p95 tail looks correlated with the batch composition for mixed-length requests (we saw a similar pattern in last quarter's benchmarks).
- The redwood_batching_config patch looks safe; it adds an adaptive cap for batches when long-sequence fraction > 18%. Worth canarying.

I can own the batching-window test (increase +15ms) and will instrument the canary with extra tracing to break down per-token compute vs scheduling delay. I'll push the patch to the canary at 11:00 PT today and run a 4-hour soak.

Open question for Sigma team: do you have a hard p95 SLA requirement for the close window? We can aim for 350ms but need to know how strict the threshold is before we flip fallback behavior.

On the meeting: 10:30 PT works for me.

—Marissa
Senior Performance Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Brian Sanders <brian.sanders@sigmahealth.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Emily Chen <emily.chen@sigmahealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Weekly MAP benchmarking sync — latency & throughput results

Thanks team — appreciate the data. A few quick clarifications from Sigma: 
- For the upcoming go/no-go close window we need p95 <= 400ms for the core routing path (we can tolerate up to 600ms for extremely long health-record extracts but need headroom).
- If you can get p95 down to <= 450ms in the canary within 48 hours, we're comfortable moving forward with the planned rollout cadence.

We are available at 10:30 PT. Emily will join and bring the scoring impacts folks (just in case the change affects clinical downstream).

-Brian
Director, Platform Engineering
Sigma Health

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Brian Sanders <brian.sanders@sigmahealth.com>, Emily Chen <emily.chen@sigmahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 10:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Weekly MAP benchmarking sync — latency & throughput results (ACTION ITEMS)

Thanks for the sync and the quick turnaround. Summary + owners (action items & timeline):

1) Canaries / immediate tuning (24–48h)
- Marissa: push redwood_batching_config.patch to canary at 11:00 PT and run a 4h soak; add tracing to split compute vs scheduling (due: 2026-06-15 15:00 PT).
- Dev: enable prefix caching for >512 token flows on the dedicated canary and report p95 delta (due: 2026-06-16 12:00 PT).

2) Fallback plan if p95 remains >450ms after canary (48–72h)
- Rishi: prepare a safe traffic-shift playbook to move long-sequence traffic to 4b variant; script for rollback included (due: 2026-06-18 09:00 PT).

3) Business acceptance and close timeline
- Sigma (Brian/Emily): confirm that p95 <= 450ms within 48h is acceptable for move to final close. Brian confirmed above; Emily to confirm clinically if any downstream scoring impact is tolerable.

Artifacts / where to find outputs:
- Benchmark CSV + initial notes: Drive link (https://drive.redwood.com/shared/drive/sigma-health/MAP-Docs)
- HubSpot deal with MAP milestones: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/9341/company/82342

I'll update this thread with soak results and a short decision note. If anything regresses or we see quality impacts, we'll pause the rollout and run the rollback playbook.

Thanks — Neha
summary: Weekly MAP checkpoint covering performance benchmarking for Sigma Health (DEAL-9341). Aggregate throughput met target but p95 tail exceeded SLA for long sequences. Action items assigned: Marissa to canary batching patch; Dev to enable prefix caching; Rishi to prepare fallback traffic-shift playbook. Sigma asked for p95 <= 450ms within 48 hours for go/no-go. Attachments and links provided.
